history.period: Ancient (per tradition); one source places the shrine at ~3,400 m
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the Bhairavnath Temple sits on a hillock above and ~500-800 m south of the Kedarnath Temple (sources disagree on the exact distance: 500 m, 800 m and ~1 km are all reported - verify). Bhairavnath (Bhukund Bhairav, a fierce form of Shiva) is venerated as the Kshetrapal - guardian and protector of Kedarnath Dham and the whole Kedar valley; tradition holds that he watches over the shrine through the winter when Kedarnath is closed, and a symbolic ritual before the annual closing requests him to take charge. Pilgrims consider the Kedarnath yatra incomplete without darshan here, and Bhukund Bhairav is worshipped before the doors of the main temple are opened each season. Mustard oil is a common offering. The spot gives a panoramic view of the entire Kedarnath valley. Coordinates use the Kedarnath Temple pin - the geocoder cannot resolve the Bhairavnath shrine itself; the temple is ~500-800 m to the south on the hill (verify exact pin).

name: Bhairavnath Temple, Kedarnath
town: Kedarnath (on the hillock above/south of the Kedarnath Temple)
town_description: Kedarnath, in Rudraprayag district at ~3,584 m, is the most remote and the highest of the Char Dham shrines, set on the bank of the Mandakini river amid the Kedar massif. Accessible only by a ~16-19 km trek from Gaurikund (or helicopter), the town comes alive in the yatra season and is abandoned in winter when the temple closes.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, ~250 km (per yatradham.org; verify)
travel.road: Road to Gaurikund, then ~16 km trek to Kedarnath; from the Kedarnath Temple a further ~500-800 m climb (verify) up the hillock to the shrine

visitor_information.best_time: May-June and September-October, same season as Kedarnath (shrine accessible only when the Kedarnath yatra is open)
